clue.text: Suitable to include Royal Society in describing this clue

indicators.note: to include says the abbreviation goes inside the word for suitable

parts.note: fit means suitable
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's national academy of sciences

explanation.surface: A setter asking whether a learned society belongs in the clue's description.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: 1 Across is the opening clue of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: This clue is numbered 1 and sits at the start, so the word for the opening position describes it.

clue.text: Enthusiast, hugging wife with son, cringes to seek favour

indicators.note: hugging means the word for enthusiast wraps around the letter for wife

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A devotee, embracing a spouse and child, grovels for approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter obsequiously, toadying for someone's approval.

clue.text: Managed Church farm

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A church that ran a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, typically for raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Disturbing spectre enveloping man — leading to these?

definitions.text: Disturbing spectre enveloping man — leading to these?

indicators.note: enveloping means the jumbled letters wrap around the word for man
disturbing means the letters of spectre are stirred up out of order

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A ghost wrapping itself around someone would give anyone the shivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a ghostly figure closing in is exactly what would produce this feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the creeps means feeling fear or unease, just what a looming phantom causes.

clue.text: New opening for old Lancashire mill town creates competition

indicators.note: New says the town's first letter is swapped for a fresh one

parts.note: Bacup is a former cotton-mill town in Lancashire, north-west England

indicators.note: the opening of the word for is its first letter

explanation.surface: A northern mill town gets a fresh start and launches a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New opening for' reads as a phrase, but 'opening for' supplies F, which replaces the B at the front of BACUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Football Association Challenge Cup is English football's oldest knockout tournament.

clue.text: Ancient Roman calendar showing period without food on island

parts.note: a fast is a time of abstaining from food

explanation.surface: A Roman almanac recording time spent hungry on an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The fasti were Roman lists of days on which business could lawfully be done, and of officials.

clue.text: With great care, search clubs mob organised

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: organised means the letters of mob are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A careful hunt through clubs that a gang has arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as a comb passes through every strand.

clue.text: Little money for girl

definitions.meaning: a small coin, so a tiny sum

explanation.surface: A small sum set aside for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny is a small coin, and Penny a short form of Penelope.

clue.text: Period noted regularly in diary

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of diary, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A span of time recorded at intervals in a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A day is a standard unit of time, a period of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Disadvantage of French river this person's admitted

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: admitted means the contraction is let into the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
the setter refers to themselves, and 'this person is' contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A drawback of a French waterway that lets the setter in.
explanation.definitionFit: A detriment is harm or damage, so a disadvantage suffered.

clue.text: Child's turn? Yes, go freely

definitions.note: read as 'child is', so the definition is the noun child

indicators.note: freely says the letters move about without fixed order

explanation.surface: A child gets a go in a game and eagerly takes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, a child.

clue.text: They succeeded Wrens in shake-up

indicators.note: a shake-up reorganises things, so the letters of wrens and in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Birds, or naval women, follow on after a reorganisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeded' tempts as 'came after', but here it means 'triumphed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who succeeded in a contest are the victors; here also the theme's cup-holders.

clue.text: Godlike spirit of strange mountain? Not quite

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are rearranged into something odd
not quite means the word mountain falls one letter short of complete

explanation.surface: A mysterious deity of an odd peak, with a hesitant qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final N, leaving MOUNTAI, which 'strange' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitou is the Algonquian name for a supernatural spirit or divine power.

clue.text: Shape of shop, dire, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Describing the sorry state of a dreadful little store.
explanation.definitionFit: A spheroid is a geometric solid, a near-sphere, so a kind of three-dimensional form.

clue.text: Sort dropping English — at home with good keyboard skill

indicators.note: dropping means the letter for English is let fall from the word

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
in means at home

explanation.surface: A kind of person, losing their Englishness, stays home to practise typing.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a keyboard competently is a skill learned by office workers and writers.

clue.text: Gossip is too much for former East German

indicators.note: the word gossip is more than the answer, holding it with a letter spare at each end

explanation.surface: Chatter overwhelms someone from the old GDR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossi was the colloquial German term for an East German, especially after reunification.

clue.text: 1A 4A 9 having answer rewritten, to accommodate the German

indicators.note: to accommodate means the shuffled letters house the German article
rewritten means the word answer is set down again in a new order

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A cross-reference demanding a reworked answer that makes room for a German.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references read FIRST FA CUP WINNERS; 'rewritten' gives WANERS from the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wanderers, a London amateur club, won the inaugural FA Cup final in 1872.

clue.text: Source, average over time, becoming anxious to please

parts.note: a well is a source of water
mean is an arithmetic average

explanation.surface: A spring, middling over time, turns eager to oblige.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-meant is offered with good intentions, eager to do right by others.

clue.text: Some lacking cover having trust as at outset new insurance arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out afresh in a new order
at outset means taking the first letter of new and of insurance

explanation.surface: Uninsured people trust a new policy set up from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking cover' looks like insurance talk but means unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists are nudists, people who go without clothing.

clue.text: Evasive conclusion of article on cathedral city

indicators.note: the conclusion of article means its final letter

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: An elusive ending to a piece about a cathedral town.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is slippery and hard to hold, so eely means elusive and shifty.

clue.text: Clumsy writer going wrong way in Italian

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in vermouth

indicators.note: going the wrong way says the word for writer runs backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An awkward author heading off course while in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong way' reverses the writer, giving NEP; 'in' places that inside the Italian abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, so awkward or clumsy in action.

clue.text: Drink knocked back first of December at sea maybe?

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for knocking them off; taken as rejected, put on ice, here

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of December

parts.note: the sea is an example of water

explanation.surface: A drink downed early in December while on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking jargon for downing the drink; it supplies the frozen-water word, with the December letter after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Water with ice in it is a cold beverage.

clue.text: Chance introducing American water lily

indicators.note: introducing places the word for chance before the abbreviation

parts.note: lot means chance or fate, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: A random moment brings an American aquatic plant into view.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a sacred aquatic plant, related to and often grouped with water lilies.

clue.text: 4A 9 in 2021, famous jockey said

indicators.note: said means the jockey's name is heard spoken

parts.note: Lester Piggott was a celebrated British flat-racing jockey

explanation.surface: Naming the 2021 cup holders through a renowned rider's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester City beat Chelsea in the 2021 final to take the trophy for the first time.

clue.text: Moral, reforming willingly in beginning in Bucks town from 1A 4A 7A

indicators.note: reforming means the letters of moral are formed again in a new order
in beginning means taking only the first letter of willingly

explanation.surface: Ethics reformed voluntarily from the start, in a home-counties town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county north-west of London. 'reforming' rearranges MORAL into MARLO. Marlow played on the first FA Cup day in 1871.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlow is a Thames-side town in Buckinghamshire whose club took part in the very first round.

clue.text: Small amount at one time limiting university

indicators.note: limiting means the phrase's word encloses the university letter

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

explanation.surface: A tiny quantity once kept a university in check.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, so a little of something.

clue.text: Like net company associated with socialist, Sidney, in past

indicators.note: in says the socialist's surname sits inside the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
Sidney Webb was a Fabian socialist and co-founder of the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A firm partnered with a famous Fabian in bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobweb is a spider's web, so something cobwebby resembles a fine mesh of threads.

clue.text: Parent losing head — something else!

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the parent's word is dropped

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A parent losing their temper is quite something!
explanation.walkthrough: 'something else!' is slang for remarkable, but the definition is the plain sense: another thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different or additional, i.e. something distinct from what was mentioned.

clue.text: Faith in Jedi, a habit brought up

indicators.note: brought up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A religion as a Star Wars knight's raised-from-youth habit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'brought up' means read upwards, i.e. backwards; 'in' marks the letters lying within the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baha'i faith is a monotheistic religion founded in nineteenth-century Persia.

clue.text: Americans' military vehicles' temperature turning to variable

definitions.note: read as 'Americans are', so the definition is the plural noun

indicators.note: turning to means one letter changes into another

parts.note: tanks are armoured military vehicles
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: US army vehicles' heat turning variable.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanks is an informal term for Americans, from Yankee.

clue.text: Uninteresting form of horse racing

explanation.surface: A dull kind of horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat racing runs on level turf without hurdles, as opposed to National Hunt jumping.

clue.text: 4A 9 most often in military store

definitions.meaning: ... have won the FA Cup more times than any other club
a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.surface: The most frequent cup holders kept in an army depot.
explanation.definitionFit: The London club takes its name from the Royal Arsenal at Woolwich, a weapons depot.

clue.text: Slight problem in Herts town from 1A 4A 7A

parts.note: a hitch is a minor snag

explanation.surface: A minor snag in a Hertfordshire town on a famous footballing date.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is Hertfordshire, a county just north of London. Hitchin played on the first FA Cup day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchin is a market town in Hertfordshire whose club entered the first ever round.

clue.text: It is briefly part of treatise

indicators.note: part of means the letters are a section inside the word treatise

explanation.surface: An abbreviated statement found within a scholarly essay.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Tis is the poetic contraction of 'it is', so a shortened form of those words.

clue.text: One dining getting attention, welcoming note?

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for attention takes the note in

parts.note: ear means attention, as in lending an ear
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A diner being noticed as a message arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at a meal is consuming food, so a person who eats.

clue.text: Starts to recall eagerly in Maidenhead, splendid bubbly place

indicators.note: starts to the following words means taking each one's first letter

explanation.surface: Fond memories of a fine Thames-side town are compared with a sparkling destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a Berkshire town, another first-round FA Cup club.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is the main city of the Champagne region, famous for its sparkling wine houses.
